title: Seedling Agro - sensor inference POC jotter
content:
Meeting capture (11/03/2025) with Seedling Agro — field ops + engineering. Quick messy notes, capture gotchas, constraints, next steps. Owner: Aisha (redwood). Attendees: Tom Ellis (Seedling CTO), Priya Rao (Field Ops lead), Jonah R (Redwood SE), Marta K (Redwood systems). Tone: whiteboard -> actionables.

Problem statement / ask:
- Seedling wants a small-footprint inference agent on solar-powered buoys used across microplots. Primary goal: on-device alerting for pest/disease patterns from intermittent camera + humidity/time-series. Must be able to run on ARM64 eMMC devices (4–8GB RAM), offline-first, periodic sync to VPC.
- Need quick POC to validate latency/cost tradeoffs and false positive rates vs cloud baseline.

Technical constraints noted:
- Devices: ODroid-C4-like (ARM64), limited RAM, no GPU. Battery budget tight: inference wakeup every 5–10 minutes max.
- Connectivity: opportunistic LTE (mostly 2–3 hours/day), long tails of no connectivity.
- Data sensitivity: crop IP + location, client prefers VPC-only storage for sync.
- Throughput: typical single-image + small sensor bundle per inference. Some frames may be pre-filtered on-device (motion detect).

Red flags / gotchas called out:
- Quantization: 8-bit dynamic quant still causes per-class score drift vs fp16 baseline — we should include small calibration set from Seedling to tune thresholds.
- KV cache irrelevant here (not autoregressive), but model size matters for cold start memory spikes. Need streaming-friendly startup (lazy-load model shards).
- Filesystem: eMMC wear — avoid frequent writes; prefer append-only log and batch sync.
- Failover: when device offline, we must surface actionable alerts locally (UI/LED + queued alert blob) and avoid double-alerts on resync.
- Time sync: several devices have drift ~10s -> can break temporal features. Use periodic NTP on LTE window.

POC approach (proposal) — rough:
1) Baseline cloud evaluation: run their labelled crop images through hosted model A (resnet-ish opt model) to measure baseline precision/recall and latency. (INF-3421 created)
2) Edge-footprint candidate: pick two compressed variants: a) quantized tiny conv model (~10–18MB) b) distill+prune variant (~6–9MB). Measure accuracy drop vs baseline with client calibration set (1000 labelled images).
3) Build minimal agent container for ARM64 that:
   - loads model lazily (stream model shards),
   - keeps inference memory < 5GB (target 3GB),
   - supports local motion prefilter,
   - batches sensor+image for single inference call.
4) Sync plan: TLS -> VPC endpoint ( customer's private VPC peering ) with message queue (SQS-like) and digest API on Redwood private plane. Backoff/retry rules and dedupe on seq id.

Metrics we'll capture in POC:
- Per-frame latency (cold start and steady-state)
- Energy per inference (mJ) estimate via device profiling
- False positive rate delta vs cloud baseline after quantization
- Sync reliability (success % per device per day)

Open questions (need follow-ups):
- Tom: can Seedling provide 1000 labelled samples for calibration by 11/10? (ACTION: Tom)
- Priya: confirm list of device SKUs (ODroid vs Pine64 variants) and exact RAM/flash; we have a tentative list but need serial models by 11/07. (ACTION: Priya)
- Security: client wants KMS-managed keys in their VPC for dead-letter blobs — need to map to Redwood Private options (Aisha to loop in security).
- Regulatory: any country-level export constraints on model weights? Tom to check (ACTION: Tom).

Immediate next steps (short timeline):
- By 11/05: Jonah to spin up baseline evaluation script, run 200 sample images from Seedling (if they can share sample subset) using hosted model A, report precision/recall. Link: JIRA SENS-129.
- By 11/07: Marta to prototype lazy-load model loader for ARM64 and run memory smoke test on emulator + one ODroid unit.
- 11/10: sync call to review calibrated thresholds and energy profiling results.

Notes to self (misc):
- Consider adding a tiny on-device confidence calibration layer (temperature scaling using small heldout set) — cheap and often fixes quantized score shifts.
- Could use a threshold-of-count window (e.g., 3 positive frames in 15 min) to reduce false positives in noisy lighting.
- Watch out for JPEG artifacts from cheap cams causing corners -> use slight gaussian blur + augment during calibration.

Slack refs / links: #solutions-seedling, thread TS-203 (attached sample images), Confluence doc for POC plan.

End of jotter — keep loose, will polish into a proper POC brief once we have sample set and device list.

Action owners recap:
- Tom Ellis (Seedling): supply 1000 labelled samples (or 200 sample subset) by 11/10, confirm export constraints.
- Priya Rao (Seedling): device SKUs + one ODroid unit for testing by 11/07.
- Jonah Rivera (Redwood): baseline eval + results by 11/05.
- Marta Kovac (Redwood): ARM64 lazy-load prototype + memory smoke by 11/07.
- Aisha Patel (Redwood): security intro and map KMS/VPC sync options by 11/09.
